title: Theory of spin-wave transport in ferromagnet-superconductor heterostructures: Negative refraction, perfect imaging and temperature-controlled spin-wave optics
authors: Tomas T. Osterholt, Thijs van der Meer, Pim H. Vree, Merel A. Bouma, Michael Borst, Toeno van der Sar, Rembert A. Duine
abstract: We investigate spin-wave transport in ferromagnetic insulator-superconductor (FMI-SC) heterostructures and develop a general theoretical framework for spin-wave optics in these hybrid systems. We demonstrate that Meissner screening by the superconductor gives rise to a range of unconventional wave phenomena, including negative phase- and group-velocity refraction, and reflection and refraction laws that differ fundamentally from their optical counterparts. Within this framework, we derive the spin-wave Fresnel equations governing reflection and transmission at FMI-SC interfaces and show that the scattering properties exhibit a pronounced temperature dependence, enabling tunable spin-wave mirrors and refractive elements. Most strikingly, we find that superconducting screening can produce nearly straight isofrequency contours, far flatter than the kinked, intrinsically curved contours attainable in conventional dipolar spin-wave systems. We show that these straight contours enable functionalities such as perfect spin-wave imaging, efficient waveguiding, and interferometric elements, such as phase shifters and beam splitters, with unconventional properties. Our results establish FMI-SC heterostructures as a versatile platform for temperature-tunable spin-wave optics and interferometric magnonic devices.
summary: This theoretical work investigates spin-wave transport in ferromagnet/superconductor heterostructures, establishing a framework based on self-consistent field calculations. The key finding is that superconducting screening induces unconventional wave phenomena, such as negative refraction and flat dispersion contours. This positions FMI-SC systems as highly versatile platforms for temperature-tunable magnonic devices.
main_problem: The study develops a general theoretical framework for spin-wave optics in Ferromagnet-Superconductor (FMI-SC) heterostructures to understand unconventional wave phenomena.
main_result: The superconducting screening leads to negative refraction and nearly straight isofrequency contours, enabling functionalities like perfect imaging and temperature-tunable magnonic devices.
method: The authors derived self-consistent equations for the total magnetic field by coupling Maxwell's equations with London equations, solving for the spin-wave dispersion relation $\omega(k)$.
model_or_system: The system is an FMI-SC heterostructure where spin waves propagate. The superconducting response modifies the effective magnetic field via Meissner screening currents.
key_observables: Negative phase/group-velocity refraction, reflection/transmission coefficients ($R_{ij}, T_{ij}$), and temperature dependence of scattering properties.
important_parameters: London penetration depth ($\lambda_L$), spin-wave wavelength ($\lambda$), film thickness ($d$), and operating temperature (near $T_c$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the quasi-static approximation, assuming thin magnetic films ($kd \ll 1$), and decomposing the total field into dipolar and screening components.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the FMI-SC heterostructure setup involving spin wave propagation and Meissner screening effects.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the general theoretical framework, deriving self-consistent equations for the magnetic field, solving for the dispersion relation, and finally analyzing boundary conditions to find reflection/transmission coefficients in different limits.
why_interesting: While focused on magnonics, the concept of using superconducting screening to engineer wave propagation (e.g., achieving flat isofrequency contours) shares conceptual parallels with engineered metamaterials used in quantum optics or cavity QED for controlling light-matter interactions.
